 No. 6 Pilots Men's Soccer to Host Selection Show Watch Party Monday at the Pilot House!
 Story Links
 Fans and media are encouraged to join Portland Pilots Men's Soccer as they find out their postseason path during the 2026 NCAA Men's Soccer Tournament selection show. Monday's watch party will take place at the Pilot House at 10 a.m. Join the team as they await their postseason fate!
 UNIVERSITY OF PORTLAND WATCH PARTY DETAILS
Date:  Monday, Nov. 16
 Time(s):  10 AM – Selection Show (NCAA.com)
 Where:  Pilot House, University of Portland, 5000 N. Willamette Blvd, Portland, OR 97203
 What:  Join Portland Pilots Men's Soccer as they learn their postseason path for the 2026 NCAA Tournament. Players, coaches and administrators will be available for interviews upon request.
 ABOUT THE PILOTS 
 The No. 6 Portland Pilots are the West Coast Conference champions twice over, having won both the WCC regular season title and the inaugural 2026 WCC Men's Soccer Championships. The Pilots are officially the first team to pull off the WCC double.
 The Pilots defeated the No. 19 San Diego Toreros 3-2 to win the WCC Tournament on Saturday and claimed the regular season title with two weeks to spare back on Oct. 24. It's the first time the Pilots have won a WCC title since 2016.
 With their tournament title, the Pilots earned an automatic bid to the NCAA Tournament. This is the 21 st time the Pilots have qualified for the tourney and the seventh time under head coach Nick Carlin-Voigt.
 Last season, the Pilots earned a first-round bye for the NCAA Tournament and advanced to the Elite Eight for the second time since 2022 and the fourth time in program history. 
 Portland has won their last 12 matches in a row and are unbeaten in their last 14 matches. It is currently the longest win streak in the nation.
 Their win streak is also the longest for the program since the 1988 season.
 The Pilots have posted a 13-3-2 record overall this year and was a perfect 8-0-0 in regular season WCC play.
 This is the first time the Pilots have posted back-to-back seasons of 13 wins or more since the 2001 and 2002 seasons.
 The Pilots were the first team to post a perfect record with no draws in WCC play since 2019 and the first team to reach eight WCC wins since 2012.
 The Pilots nearly swept the WCC Postseason Awards, with Carlin-Voigt winning Coach of the Year, David Ajagbe winning Offensive Player of the Year, Joe Highfield Midfielder of the Year, Nikos Clarke-Tosczak Defender of the Year and Miguel-Angel Hernandez Goalkeeper of the Year.
 The Pilots entered the weekend in the top 10 nationally in numerous categories, sitting at third in points per game (8.5), fourth in assists per game (3.24) and total assists (59), fifth in goals per game (2.61) and total goals (47) and sixth in total points (153).
